One basin, many purchase orders: how Los Angeles NDT shops end up under NAS 410 or SNT-TC-1A

The Los Angeles basin holds one of the country's deepest aerospace supply bases, and few of its companies build whole aircraft. They forge, cast, machine, heat treat, plate, bond and test parts for primes and tier-one suppliers across the country. Weber Metals in Paramount, for example, forges aluminum and titanium structural components for commercial and military aircraft and jet engines, and lists penetrant and sonic inspection among its own processes. Around plants like that sit independent test labs and special process houses serving dozens of customers at once. For their NDT people, the scheme question can have two answers inside one building.

How a purchase-order clause becomes your certification standard

NAS 410 is an Aerospace Industries Association standard with mandatory minimums, but only once a contract, purchase order or customer quality clause invokes it. Airframe and engine makers commonly write NAS 410, or EN 4179 for European customers, into those clauses, and each tier passes the requirement to the shop that inspects the hardware. A Paramount forge or a Gardena machine shop may therefore certify its penetrant inspectors to NAS 410 because of one customer's terms, often alongside Nadcap accreditation for the method. The employer still certifies each person, under a written practice controlled by a Responsible Level 3 (RL3).

Special process houses and labs: two programs under one roof

A basin test lab can inspect aerospace castings in the morning and structural welds for a downtown tower in the afternoon. The aerospace work follows whatever the customer's clause names, usually NAS 410; the seismic UT and MT on building steel, and refinery work in Wilmington, follow AWS and ASME practice under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. A lab running both should certify under clearly separate sections or separate written practices, name the standard and revision on every certification, and keep training records to the stricter NAS 410 evidence standard so a technician's file supports either scheme. An SNT-TC-1A certificate never answers a NAS 410 requirement on its own.

A checklist for technicians changing employers in the basin

  1. Ask the hiring Level 3 which standard and revision the written practice cites, and whether NAS 410 Revision 6, released in December 2025, is in force there yet.
  2. Bring course outlines with hours and instructor names. An RL3 decides what to credit from evidence, not from a certificate's title.
  3. Coming from field work, expect gap training in penetrant and magnetic particle; NAS 410 asks for more formal surface-method training than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  4. Show experience by product form: forgings, castings, machined parts, welds. The penetrant testing of castings guide and the forging and casting UT guide show what aerospace shops look for.
  5. Keep copies of your examinations and vision records. Certification ends when the job does; the evidence stays with you.

For quality managers preparing for a Nadcap AC7114 audit

Nadcap accredits the NDT process at a site; it does not certify people. Its auditors pick names off signed reports and trace them back through training, experience, examinations, vision checks and the RL3's approvals, and a broken link in that trail is written up as a finding. Shops that grew their aerospace work quickly should test their own files before an auditor does. Atlantis offers NAS 410 audit documentation support in Los Angeles: we draft and review the files, and your RL3 signs them off.

What Atlantis offers Los Angeles aerospace employers

Aerospace and aviation work gets the full Atlantis offer: ASNT NDT Level III consulting (written practices on SNT-TC-1A aligned with customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, procedures, Level I and II examinations, outside agency Level III services in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT), SNT-TC-1A-based training, and UT, MT, PT and VT inspection. Training means self-paced online theory with Level III answers to your questions, rehearsal in the Practical NDT simulator, and the practical examination at your employer's facility. We have no Los Angeles classroom. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to any Los Angeles shop. If you hope outside training will count toward a NAS 410 certification, get your employer's RL3 to confirm it first. For the full comparison read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A; nearby, the El Segundo, Long Beach and Palmdale pages cover the space, launch and flight-test corners of the region.
